label: Dismantled Neo-Confucian nannü hierarchy as the root of all social oppression
description: He-Yin Zhen launched a foundational philosophical assault on Confucian ritual hierarchy (nannü differentiation), demonstrating that classifying human beings into superior/inferior sexed roles anchored state and property domination.
dialecticalTension: Exposes patriarchal hierarchy not as timeless moral order but as historical domination.
historicalContext: Published in Tianyi bao (Natural Justice), Tokyo, 1907–1908.

citations.author: He-Yin Zhen
citations.work: On the Question of Women's Liberation (1907)

label: Combined socialist critique of private property with primacy of nannü domination
description: Engaging socialist and Marxist translations circulating in Tokyo (including the first Chinese translation of The Communist Manifesto in Tianyi bao), He-Yin Zhen argued that patriarchy cannot be reduced merely to capitalism—both must fall together.
dialecticalTension: Refuses class-only reductionism while insisting on economic revolution for women's liberation.

citations.author: Lydia H. Liu, Rebecca E. Karl & Dorothy Ko
citations.work: The Birth of Chinese Feminism: Essential Texts in Transnational Theory

label: Formulated structural deconstruction of nannü and total anarcho-feminism
description: He-Yin Zhen conceptualized nannü as a historical regime producing gendered hierarchy prior to and alongside state-capitalist power, founding non-Western anarcho-feminist theory.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes sex/gender deconstruction with anti-statist economic egalitarianism.

label: Cross-pollinated East Asian anarcho-feminist critique of state and family law
description: Tokyo's early twentieth-century transnational anarchist milieu linked Chinese Tianyi bao writers like He-Yin Zhen with Japanese radicals like Noe Itō in a shared rejection of patriarchal family registration and state coercion.
dialecticalTension: Connects Chinese and Japanese radical critiques of East Asian state patriarchy.
